findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the sort key. With order_by='-datetime' in the audit logs endpoint, that key is a datetime, so a TypeError is raised. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting to an epoch timestamp first.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838-840, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key passes getattr(item, self.key) directly to math.floor/math.ceil, unlike DateTimePaginator.get_item_key at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:233-236 which first converts it via float(value.strftime("%s.%f")) * self.multiplier. Because src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:76-83 uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime" on AuditLogEntry (where datetime is a DateTimeField at src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69), paginating any non-empty result raises a TypeError.

findings.claim: The enable_advanced check in the audit logs endpoint accesses organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check. member is None for callers without membership, such as superusers, API keys/org auth tokens, legacy org ApiKeys and internal-integration proxy users, so an AttributeError is raised.

verifier.reason: At src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71, the patch adds `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` without checking if `organization_context.member` is `None` (typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None` at src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:298). Although superusers short-circuit on `request.user.is_superuser`, non-member callers with `org:write` such as `OrgAuthToken` (src/sentry/api/authentication.py:456-484), legacy `ApiKey` (src/sentry/api/authentication.py:258-286), and SentryApp/internal-integration proxy users (src/sentry/auth/access.py:1007-1027) have `request.user.is_superuser == False` and `organization_context.member is None`, causing an `AttributeError` on every GET request.

findings.claim: When enable_advanced_features is true, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a user-supplied negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so a crafted cursor (e.g. 0:-10:0) raises an error that is not converted to BadPaginationError and results in a 500.

verifier.reason: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the Django QuerySet directly with the negative start_offset (queryset[start_offset:stop]), which raises ValueError because Django QuerySets forbid negative indexing. Neither get_result nor Endpoint.paginate (src/sentry/api/base.py:525-540, which only catches BadPaginationError) converts this error, so an uncaught exception from a cursor like 0:-10:0 returns HTTP 500.
